scheme_name: Deep Ocean Mission – Mineral Extraction Startup
overview: Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) is a central sector scheme under the Ministry of Earth Sciences aimed at exploring and harnessing marine living and non-living resources sustainably. It focuses on deep-sea mining, ocean climate change advisory services, technological innovations for exploration, and capacity building in marine science. The mission supports startups and research in mineral extraction from the deep ocean, particularly polymetallic nodules, as part of India's Blue Economy initiatives.
objectives: Explore and harness marine living and non-living resources sustainably
Develop technologies for deep-sea mining and mineral extraction
Provide ocean climate change advisory services
Enhance capacity building in marine science and technology
Support Blue Economy initiatives including startups in mineral extraction
Conduct deep-sea biodiversity surveys and resource assessment
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, research institutions, and organizations engaged in deep-sea exploration, mineral extraction, ocean technology development, and related Blue Economy activities are eligible to participate under the Deep Ocean Mission, subject to project proposals aligning with mission objectives and guidelines issued by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, access to deep-sea data and samples, technical collaboration with MoES-affiliated institutions (NIOT, NCPOR, INCOIS, IITM), infrastructure support for testing and validation, policy and regulatory guidance, and recognition under national Blue Economy frameworks.
financial_support: Funding is provided through competitive grant-based mechanisms for approved projects under the Deep Ocean Mission, with financial assistance sanctioned as per the Detailed Demands for Grants and annual budget allocations of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, subject to project appraisal and approval by the competent authority.
application_process: 1. Identify project area aligned with Deep Ocean Mission objectives such as mineral exploration, ocean technology, or marine resource assessment. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including technical feasibility, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated channel of the Ministry of Earth Sciences. 4. Proposal undergoes technical and financial appraisal by expert committees. 5. Upon approval, enter into a memorandum of understanding or agreement with MoES. 6. Receive funds in installments as per project milestones. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 8. Final project completion report and asset disclosure upon conclusion.
required_documents: Undertaking of compliance with environmental and safety norms
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability and review cycles.
caveats: Funding is subject to availability of budget under the Deep Ocean Mission
Projects must comply with international seabed authority regulations and environmental norms
Intellectual property rights may be shared as per government-funded project guidelines
Utilization certificates and audit reports are mandatory for fund release
Continued funding depends on satisfactory progress and outcomes
